content.title: Where Is Morgan Metzer, Subject of 'Gaslit By My Husband,' Now?
content.text: This story discusses sexual violence and abuse. If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Telephone Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 or the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-SAFE (1-800-799-7233).The harrowing journey of Morgan Metzer that ultimately empowered her to help other women facing domestic violence issues began in 2021 on New Year’s Day. Metzer was beaten and sexually assaulted by a masked man in the bedroom of her Georgia home and left tied up with a pillowcase on her head. Shortly afterward, her ex-husband, Rodney Metzer, arrived to help her and was distraught over what happened. Eventually the truth came out: Rodney, the father of their twins, was the one who had assaulted her. Metzer’s story was dramatized in the 2024 movie, “Gaslit By My Husband: The Morgan Metzer Story.” The film, starring actor and singer Jana Kramer as Metzer, originally aired on Lifetime and has now found a new audience as one of the most-watched movies on Netflix. “This one was a tough story to step into…emotionally heavy and deeply real, but it was also incredibly meaningful to tell and healing for my past,” Kramer wrote on Instagram on March 16 upon the film’s release on Netflix. “Getting to film this alongside my daughter made it even more special, and sharing scenes with one of my favorite scene partners, @austinnichols made the experience that much better.”“Stories like this matter,” she continued. “Because sometimes the hardest truths are the ones that help people feel less alone. If this film reminds even one person to trust their voice and their strength, then it was worth telling.”What Happened to Morgan Metzer? At about 12:30 a.m. on Jan. 1, 2021, Metzer was assaulted by a masked attacker in her bedroom who struck her with the butt of his gun and tried to strangle her, according to a news release by the Office of the District Attorney for the Blue Ridge Judicial Circuit in Canton, Georgia. The assailant zip tied her hands and then sexually assaulted her, all the while disguising his voice. He followed by putting a pillowcase over her head, dragging her to the deck of the house and leaving her there face down, according to the district attorney’s office. He told her not to move until she heard a car honk or he would shoot her. Rodney Metzer then arrived, found his ex-wife on the deck and called 911 at about 2 a.m., according to the district attorney’s office. He appeared on the front porch looking like “a concerned family member,” per the news release. A subsequent investigation revealed that Rodney Metzer had been the one who assaulted his wife, one day after he had come to her house and tried to reconcile with her. The couple, who shared two children, had recently gotten divorced. Following the assault, Rodney went to his apartment, got changed and went back to Morgan’s home to find her face down and tied up. An investigation by the Cherokee Sheriff’s Office found a handgun in Rodney’s vehicle and his zip ties in his apartment that matched the ones used to bind Morgan, according to the district attorney’s office. Rodney was also seen on surveillance video leaving a Lowe’s Home Improvement store with a pack of zip ties and on a separate surveillance video entering his apartment and leaving shortly after wearing different clothes. Police also investigated his online search history and found searches for “how long before you starve to death,” “how to change the sound of your voice,” and “how long it takes to choke someone unconscious.” The film now showing on Netflix not only depicts the assault on Metzer but also how her ex-husband gaslit her for years to the point where she was questioning reality. Played by Austin Nichols of “One Tree Hill” in the movie, he is shown telling little lies to get Metzer to question reality, like saying he had told her to pick up their children from school when he hadn’t. In another scene, he pushes her down the stairs and later convinces her that she pushed him down the stairs instead. “I want them to know it’s not big stuff. It could be very minimal,” Morgan Metzer told TODAY.com about gaslighting in 2024. “It could add up … piece by piece.”“Check yourself with every argument or every situation that arises,” she continued. “Generally go, ‘OK, was I at fault? Did I not do this?’ And then don’t let it chip away until it gets big.”Kramer, who has spoken about experiencing domestic violence, described the feeling of being gaslit. “Manipulation is the biggest thing in gaslighting,” she told TODAY.com in 2024. “They can manipulate you to think anything, and it’s going to turn into guilt. So then typically you hide from your guilt. You don’t want to share your problems out loud. You are not going to go and tell somebody, ‘Oh, my husband and I did this.’ So then you keep it all inside, and you think you’re the bad person.”Assistant District Attorney Rachel Ashe called Rodney Metzer “a master manipulator” in the news release and said he also faked a cancer diagnosis a few days before the attack to try to gain his ex-wife’s sympathy. Where Is Morgan Metzer Now? Metzer has been sharing her story with the hope of helping others in abusive relationships. “If I don’t take the bad that came of this, that I feel that God wants me to do, it’s like, why did it happen,” Metzer told TODAY.com in 2024. “It would happen for no reason. I’ve got to take the pain and turn that into something that’s powerful to help women.”One struggle was feeling like she was all alone in trying to break free from her ex-husband. “It feels very isolating when you’re in a gaslighting abusive relationship that you’re the only one, or you’re crazy or it’s your fault,” she told TODAY.com. “And I hope people find their voice after watching this to know that they’re not alone and that there is help out there.”She also advocates for women opening up to one another about what’s honestly going on in their relationships. “The biggest thing is women need to trust each other,” she said. “Stop trying to make it look like everything is absolutely perfect. You’ve got the perfect husband, you’ve got the perfect life. You’ve got the perfect kids. If you would speak to each other, your friends would see the signs first, and you could get out earlier.”Where Is Rodney Metzer Now? He pled guilty in 2021 to 14 charges, including kidnapping, sexual battery and aggravated assault, according to a news release.He was sentenced to 70 years in prison, with the first 25 years to be served in confinement and the remaining 45 years on probation. Metzer is currently incarcerated in Baldwin State Prison in Milledgeville, Georgia, according to inmate records from the Georgia Department of Corrections.
